subject: Information-architecture / layout reorganization of the Weather card (#card-weather / renderWeather at viewer.html:6568, renderWeatherSummary:6557, renderRainfallPanel:6471, renderAmbientStationPanel:6241, computeBurnStatus:13151, generateGardenerInsight:6071)
scope_note: IA + layout only, per the split with user-researcher (who is framing reader jobs separately). This review does not re-derive the jobs; it takes the glance/repository principle + the fishing A-G precedent as the design spine and maps the weather card onto it.

user_context.primary_user: Two readers share this card (unlike fishing, which was Paul-only): (1) Mom — the confirmed daily user (memory: analyze-fernwood rollup; Mom-no-glasses a11y applies), glancing to know 'what's it doing outside'; (2) Paul — same read plus the burn/rain/pressure detail. The card must serve the calm-glance reader first and let the detail reader drill in.
core_jobs_to_be_done: At a glance: what is it doing outside right now, and is there anything I should know about today? (decision layer)
Read the true CURRENT conditions from the on-property station — one clean measured read, not blended with a model
See what's coming — today's high/low, the next few days, the next hours (forecast, clearly a forecast)
Drill into recent + coming rainfall, indoor sensors, burn/fire rules, and where the data comes from (reference)
user_context.context_of_use: Phone, on or away from the property, glancing at the Fernwood dashboard. Field-journal tone — 'looking out at the land,' never an ops console. No urgency language (project tone rule).
assumptions_made: Weather is a general-audience card (Mom + Paul), not Paul-tactical like fishing — so the calm-glance discipline and Mom-legibility bar apply here where they were exempted on the fishing card.

The on-site Ambient station is the freshest, most-local source; Open-Meteo is the modeled layer; ERA5 is reference plumbing (matches CLAUDE.md source-hierarchy: station -> forecast -> season/reference).

principles_applied: The glance and the repository (CLAUDE.md governing principle) — decision layer up top, reference relocated down, nothing deleted
Freshness sets altitude (cross-project.md) — order by how live/local a signal is; the constant static ban is the LOWEST-altitude signal on the card
Source-hierarchy drives layout (cross-project.md) — station -> forecast -> season/reference
Trust is load-bearing; measured signals kept visually distinct from modeled (CLAUDE.md; fishing R2) — a modeled read must not borrow the station's authority
One engine, one verdict (fernwood.md, from 2026-07-06 fishing reorg) — the header summary and the in-card summary must be driven by one generator so they can never disagree
Nielsen #4 consistency; Nielsen #1 visibility of system status

findings.observation: Four separate 'what's going on now' reads coexist, from three different sources: (a) the collapsed-header summary #weather-summary via renderWeatherSummary() = Open-Meteo cur.temperature + cur.condition + worst alert (MODELED temp); (b) the in-card 'Today' gardener insight = generateGardenerInsight(), which is station-PREFERRED synthesized prose ('Mild comfortable afternoon — 68F at the property'); (c) the 'Right now' station hero headline (MEASURED); (d) the Open-Meteo condition word woven into 'Right now'. Temperature is stated up to four times; the sky/condition word twice.
findings.user_impact: This is the concrete source of Paul's 'clobbered / several views of today' complaint. Worse than clutter: the header can show a MODELED Open-Meteo temp while the body shows a MEASURED station temp a few degrees different — the card visibly disagrees with itself, which erodes the trust the whole card is built on. There is no single, authoritative 'here is now' the eye can land on.
findings.principle_invoked: One engine, one verdict; Trust is load-bearing
findings.recommendation: Pick ONE current-read generator, station-first, and drive everything from it. generateGardenerInsight() is already the right one (station-preferred, calm, field-journal voice, honest 'on the forecast' fallback). Make it the single glance sentence at the top of the card body (A), and have renderWeatherSummary() call the same generator (or a compact variant) so the collapsed header and the expanded top can never disagree. The Open-Meteo condition word stops being a competing 'now' and becomes a source-tagged sky descriptor (see F3).

findings.observation: The 'Right now' block (renderWeather ~6646) fuses two sources inside one .wblock with only a margin-top:10px between them: #ambient-station-panel (MEASURED station temp/humidity/wind/rain/pressure/dew) and a weather-current-row carrying the Open-Meteo condition word + weather-icon-big + today's High/Low (MODELED). They read as one continuous 'right now' reading.
findings.user_impact: This is the exact smell Paul flagged, and the exact thing the fishing card deliberately avoided (R2, 2026-07-06: 'estimates must read as estimates at every altitude'). By sitting flush with the measured station numbers, the modeled condition + H/L borrow the station's authority — the reader can't tell which figures are ground-truth and which are a forecast. On the card whose credibility rests on 'measured, on your property,' that blur is the costliest kind.
findings.principle_invoked: Trust is load-bearing; measured kept visually distinct from modeled
findings.recommendation: Split the block. B RIGHT NOW = station hero ONLY, headed with the existing 📡 src-tag ('Measured on the property'). Move the H/L into the FORECAST block (C, modeled). Handle the condition word per F3. Reuse the existing .src-tag-station / .src-tag-forecast chips + 📡/☁️ vocabulary already defined at CSS ~1262 — do not invent new styling.

findings.observation: The Open-Meteo condition word ('Partly cloudy') is the one 'now' fact the station genuinely cannot report — the PWS has no sky-state sensor. So it isn't pure redundancy; it's a real gap the model legitimately fills. But today it is presented with measured-weight, inside the station block.
findings.user_impact: If it's simply deleted, the reader loses the sky read. If it stays fused with the station numbers, it violates F2. It needs a home that is honest about being modeled.
findings.principle_invoked: Measured distinct from modeled (the honest-split, not delete)
findings.recommendation: Give the condition word its own source-tagged line — either a distinct '☁️ Sky: partly cloudy (forecast)' sub-row at the FOOT of B (visually separated from the measured numbers), or as the lead of the FORECAST block C. Recommend the foot-of-B sub-row, since 'what does the sky look like now' is a current-moment question — but tagged ☁️ so it can't pass as a station reading.

findings.observation: Burn status sits at position 3 — above the freshest station read (position 5) and above the whole forecast. But computeBurnStatus() is almost entirely static/slow: a seasonal regulatory ban keyed only on month (inSeasonalBan, May-Sep), plus slow drought/days-since-rain context. During the ~5-month ban it shows the same 'State outdoor-burning ban active' line every single day. It is the LOWEST-freshness signal on the card, occupying near the highest altitude.
findings.user_impact: This is Paul's stated #1 fix ('the constant outdoor burn ban is static -> move to bottom'). A block that never changes is trained-blindness fuel sitting where the eye expects live news, and it pushes the actual live station read down the scroll. Freshness-sets-altitude is inverted here.
findings.principle_invoked: Freshness sets altitude; the glance and the repository (relocate depth, don't delete)
findings.recommendation: Move the burn block to the bottom reference zone (F). BUT do not blanket-bury it — see F5: the one time it IS fresh (an active NWS fire-weather alert) it must promote upward, not sit at the bottom.

findings.observation: computeBurnStatus() fuses two very different-freshness things into one block: (a) a static seasonal/regulatory baseline (the constant ban), and (b) a genuinely time-sensitive Tier-1 'severe' output driven by an active NWS Red Flag / Fire Weather alert (fwAlerts). If F4 is applied naively, moving 'burn status' to the bottom would also bury a live Red Flag warning at the bottom of the card.
findings.user_impact: Burying an active fire-weather alert is a real safety/decision miss, not just polish — it's the one weather-card output where getting the altitude wrong has consequences on a dry mountain property. The static ban and the live fire alert must not share a fate.
findings.principle_invoked: Freshness sets altitude (split the fused signal by freshness); Nielsen #1 visibility of system status
findings.recommendation: Split by freshness at the source. When burn.level === 'severe' (active fire-weather alert), surface it as an ALERT in the top 'Worth knowing' block (A) — it's decision-shaped and fresh. The normal/elevated regulatory baseline (the static ban + drought/days-dry context) goes to the bottom reference block (F). One computeBurnStatus() call, routed to two altitudes by tier.

findings.observation: The Rainfall panel (position 8) leads with the on-property station rain gauge (renderPropertyGaugeBlock — now/today/event/week/month, MEASURED, ~0.3 mi local) yet sits BELOW the 7-day and hourly forecast (modeled). The measured, local, recent-rain read is positioned as less-fresh than a multi-day model. Indoor sensors (position 9, also measured station data) sit even lower.
findings.user_impact: Same freshness-inversion as F4, milder: a measured local signal reads as reference-tier by position. On a mountain property, 'how much has actually fallen here lately' is a high-value, high-freshness glance — the gauge earns a higher altitude than it has.
findings.principle_invoked: Freshness sets altitude; source-hierarchy drives layout
findings.recommendation: Keep the Rainfall panel unified (gauge 📡 + regional/ERA5 context ☁️/📊 with its existing divider), but lift it to the glance->repository seam — after the forecast, as the 'how wet, recently and ahead' bridge into reference — OR directly after B if you want the measured gauge adjacent to current conditions. Recommend seam placement (D) for v1; it's a judgment call because the panel itself spans measured-recent through modeled-context. Indoor sensors move to the reference zone (E).

findings.observation: When the card is expanded there is no single top-of-body glance line. The reader meets, in order: source-status bar -> alerts -> burn -> 'Today' -> 'Right now' — several blocks before one clean current read. The header summary line only shows in the collapsed state; on expand it disappears and is not replaced by an equivalent anchor.
findings.user_impact: The reader expands the card wanting 'so what's it doing?' and has to assemble the answer from 3-4 blocks. The fishing card solved exactly this by opening on a verdict line (A). Weather has no equivalent single landing spot once opened.
findings.principle_invoked: The glance and the repository (the glance must lead); Meet the user at the action
findings.recommendation: Promote the single station-first summary sentence (F1) to the very top of the card body as block A, immediately under the source-status bar, with the 'Worth knowing' alerts. That IS the glance; everything below it is progressive depth.

proposed_section_order.spine: Mirrors the fishing A-G: a GLANCE zone (freshest-first, decision-shaped) -> seam -> a REPOSITORY zone (reference, slow-moving). Measured (📡) and modeled (☁️) are legibly separated throughout; the static ban lands at the bottom, its severe tier promotes to the top.

glance_zone.note: ONE summary sentence (generateGardenerInsight, also drives #weather-summary) + 'Worth knowing' alerts, INCLUDING a promoted severe fire-weather alert (F5). The single thing the eye lands on.

glance_zone.note: Station hero ONLY (temp/feels/humidity/wind/rain/dew/pressure/trends). Sky-condition word as a distinct ☁️-tagged sub-row at its foot (F3).

summary_reconciliation.problem: Three current-read surfaces, two source families: #weather-summary (header, MODELED Open-Meteo temp+condition+alert), the 'Today' gardener insight (station-PREFERRED synthesized prose), and the Open-Meteo condition word (MODELED).
summary_reconciliation.resolution: generateGardenerInsight() is the canonical current read — station-first, calm, honest fallback. (1) Promote it to the top-of-body glance (A). (2) Make renderWeatherSummary() call the same generator so the collapsed header agrees with the body (one engine, one verdict). (3) Retire the condition word as a competing 'now'; re-home it as an explicitly ☁️-tagged sky descriptor (F3). Net: exactly one authoritative current sentence, station-first, everywhere it appears.

measured_vs_modeled_discipline.reuse: The card already ships .src-tag-station / .src-tag-forecast / .src-tag-reference chips + 📡/☁️/📊 vocabulary + the top status bar (CSS ~1262-1351). Reuse them; do not invent new styling.
rules: B RIGHT NOW: header 📡 'Measured on the property'; every figure is a station reading; the ☁️ sky word sits in its own tagged sub-row, never flush with the numbers (fixes the F2 blend).
C FORECAST: header ☁️ 'Open-Meteo forecast'; H/L + 7-day + hourly all live here as one clearly-modeled zone.
D RAINFALL: 📡 gauge sub-block and ☁️/📊 regional/ERA5 sub-block kept either side of the existing divider.
A glance sentence: when it uses the forecast fallback it already says 'on the forecast' — keep that honest marker; when station-sourced it says 'at the property'.

loop_note: The Fernwood flywheel (invite ground-truth where we admit a model) is lighter on this card than on fishing, because the station already IS the ground truth for most current fields. The one honest-estimate seam is the modeled sky/condition word and the forecast — a future, optional 'does that match what you see?' invite could live at the foot of C. NOT a build ask here; flagged so the loop isn't forgotten when the reorg lands.
severity_calibration_note: Hobby project — nothing is 'critical' (no lost work; the reader can still read the weather today). The three 'important' findings are genuine trust/decision risks, not enterprise inflation: F1 (header vs body can show different temps), F2 (modeled data wearing the station's authority — the exact smell Paul named), F5 (a live fire-weather alert could get buried at the bottom). F4 is Paul's own stated fix. The rest (F3, F6, F7) are polish/placement.
open_questions_for_user: Rainfall placement: at the glance->repository seam (D, recommended) so the forecast still reads as one block, or lifted higher to sit directly under B so the measured gauge is adjacent to current conditions? The panel spans measured-recent through modeled-context, so it's a real judgment call.
Sky-condition word home: foot-of-B ☁️ sub-row (recommended — it's a current-moment question) or lead-of-C?
Do you want the promoted severe fire-weather alert (F5) to also keep a line in the bottom Burn block for continuity, or promote-only (appears at top, absent from bottom while active)?
follow_up_research_suggested: user-researcher is framing the reader jobs for this card separately — reconcile this IA against that once it lands (as was done for fishing on 2026-07-06).

principles_to_propose.principle: Split a fused block by the freshness of its parts, not by its topic — a single computed block that mixes a static baseline with a live exception must route each part to the altitude its freshness earns (static to the bottom, the live exception to the top).
principles_to_propose.rationale: computeBurnStatus() is one 'topic' (burning) but two freshnesses: a constant seasonal ban and an active fire-weather alert. Grouping by topic buried the live part; grouping by freshness fixes it. This is the next refinement of 'Freshness sets altitude' — it says the unit that gets an altitude is the SIGNAL, not the topical block, so topical blocks may need splitting. Same shape likely recurs (a 'Rainfall' block with a live gauge + a 25-year normal; a financial 'position' block with a live price + a static thesis). Propose after Paul approves the reorg.

principles_to_propose.principle: A modeled reading placed flush with a measured one inherits its authority — separate them with a source tag and visual break, or the model gets believed as ground-truth.
principles_to_propose.rationale: Second occurrence of the fishing R2 pattern (estimate dressed as reading). Here it's the Open-Meteo condition + H/L sitting inside the station hero block. Fernwood has many measured/modeled adjacencies (lake temp, rainfall, sky) and the card's whole credibility is 'measured on your property,' so the discipline is worth naming as a standing fernwood rule. Propose after the split lands.
